source.name: The combobox's aria-activedescendant must reference the highlighted suggestion element
source.scope: Real upstream bug (https://github.com/TarekRaafat/autoComplete.js/commit/ec706d39c045b3ca9a75d71546610dcf466d26a4) at de0356005310bd2af2b1a5d97add43908bac6c6f. Blind to the maintainers' fix ec706d39c045b3ca9a75d71546610dcf466d26a4; routing auto.

journey.title: Arrow through store suggestions with the active option announced
journey.goal: While arrowing through suggestions, the input's aria-activedescendant names the highlighted option element

functionalJourney.title: Choose a pickup store with the pointer
functionalJourney.goal: Clicking a suggestion fills the store field

guards.title: Arrow up from the field to the last suggestion
guards.goal: ArrowUp wraps to the last suggestion and Enter chooses it

plan.root_cause: The navigation controller incorrectly sets aria-activedescendant to the list item's data value (its label) instead of the element's ID, causing assistive technologies to announce the wrong active option during arrow key navigation.
plan.repair_strategy: In src/controllers/navigationController.js, replace the use of list[currentFocus].dataset.value with list[currentFocus].id when assigning the aria-activedescendant attribute within the update function.
plan.expected_accessibility_effect: Arrow key navigation will now correctly update the input's aria-activedescendant to reference the active listitem's ID, enabling screen readers to announce the highlighted option as expected.
functional_risks: Any custom code that erroneously relied on aria-activedescendant containing the item's label may need adjustment, but the attribute is spec‑defined to hold an ID reference, so risk is low.
verification_requirements: After typing 'ma' and pressing ArrowDown once, the input's aria-activedescendant must equal 'autoCompleteJS_result_0'.
After a second ArrowDown, it must equal 'autoCompleteJS_result_1'.
Pressing Enter must submit the form with store value ['Marina Park'].
